about.title: Personal Injury Help in Brawley, California
about.longDescription: Brawley sits at a crossroads of agricultural and commuter traffic, with Main Street, Rt 111, Rt 86, and Old Highway 111 carrying much of the town's daily flow. Public records show 38 injury collisions in the most recent year, leaving 49 people hurt and, tragically, 1 person dead. Those numbers aren't abstract — they represent neighbors, farmworkers, and families whose routines were interrupted in an instant. If you or someone you love was injured in a crash on these roads or anywhere else in the city, you may be weighing medical bills, missed work, and a claims process that feels confusing at the worst possible time. LawProactive is not a law firm. We're a free service that listens to what happened, then connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who can review your situation and explain your options under California law. There's no obligation to move forward, and if you do, the attorney works on contingency — meaning no fee unless you recover compensation. Our goal is simply to make that first step easier, so you can focus on healing instead of paperwork.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: A Filing Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on compensation entirely.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue a claim even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in typical injury cases. This matters when injuries affect daily life well beyond medical bills.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of a recovery. If there's no settlement or award, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and connecting with an independent attorney costs you nothing upfront. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. We are a connection service that helps injured people in Brawley and across Imperial County find an independent personal injury attorney. The attorney you're connected with handles the legal work, not LawProactive.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Brawley?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle, the notice window can be as short as six months, so it's worth acting promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, not blocked altogether.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Brawley?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like Main Street, Rt 111, Rt 86, and Old Highway 111, with reports often peaking on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply reported patterns from public records, not a judgment about any specific road.
